newsitem.title: INDIA: India VSNL up on BSE, NSE gains trimmed.
newsitem.headline: India VSNL up on BSE, NSE gains trimmed.

text.p: Shares of India's overseas telecommunications monopoly Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL) jumped 84.75 rupees, or 8.6 percent, to a provisional close of 1,070 on the Bombay bourse on Tuesday.
But VSNL shares erased some early gains on the National Stock Exchange (NSE). They finished 13.75 rupees higher at 985.25 -- off an early high of 1,039 rupees, dealers said.
Traders said volumes were driven by speculators who expected investors to bid in the local stock after VSNL's issue of global depositary receipts (GDRs) was oversubscribed on Monday.
"Speculators are hoping that some investors who didn't get GDR allotments could pick up the local share," said a trader at a foreign brokerage.
Traders said VSNL shares had not risen as sharply on the NSE as it was the last day of the weekly account.
VSNL said on Monday its GDR issue had been priced at $13.93 per GDR, or 1,000 rupees per VSNL share. It said in a statement the issue had been oversubscribed about 10 times.
The price represented a 1.5 percent premium to VSNL's closing price of March 21. Each GDR represents half an ordinary VSNL share.
Investment bankers said the VSNL GDR was trading sharply higher than the issue price in London at around $17.45/17.65.
"There's brisk trading in the after market," said a London-based investment banker.
